newsitem.title: HONG KONG: IPO VIEW: airline IPOs to spice up H-share market.
newsitem.headline: IPO VIEW: airline IPOs to spice up H-share market.

text.p: Listings of China-incorporated companies in Hong Kong have failed to excite the investment community here, but upcoming H-share IPOs in the airline industry should add some spice to the sector, analysts said.
H-shares are stocks of Chinese enterprises listed in Hong Kong. There are currently 21 H-shares listed, but poor earnings and a lack of transparency have plagued their performances.
"Investors are quite cautious on H-shares because of their past unsatisfactory performances," said William Lo, head of China Research at Kleinwort Benson Securities (Asia) Ltd.
"Unless their quality and fundamentals are sound and exciting, investors will not be interested," he said.
Most H-share firms are in the industrial sector, and upcoming issues are mainly focused on infrastructure and power supply. Analysts said airlines were considered more exciting.
"I think high-tech, airlines and consumer products related (H-shares) issues will be more attractive to investors," said Sunny Chan, research manager at Seapower Research.
"Fund managers like high-tech and airlines stocks very much," he said.
Investors are eagerly awaiting the listing of China Eastern Airlines, which is expected to seek a dual listing in Hong Kong and the United States by the end of 1996 or in early 1997.

"European and the U.S. investors are expected to favour airlines stocks because they know more about the operations and overall business of the industry," said Michael Ng, analyst at ASG Investment said.
Another airline operator, China Southern Airlines, is also expected to seek a listing in the first quarter of 1997.
However, the next H-share issue will be toll road operator Anhui Expressway Co Ltd, and analysts predicted only moderate interest. The shares are due to begin trading on November 13.
Anhui offered 493.01 million H-shares at HK$1.77 per share, of which 73.95 million shares were offered in Hong Kong. The Hong Kong IPO was only 1.04 times subscribed.
"Its fundamentals don't sound exciting due to its existing asset of only one toll road," said an analyst at local brokerage.
Anhui currently owns and operates the 134-km Hening (Hefei-Nanjing) Expressway in Anhui Province. It said it would use part of the IPO proceeds to buy the Tianchang section of National Highway 205.

Also coming up are Beijing Datang Power Generation Co, which is expected to seek a dual listing in Hong Kong and London in early December, and Shandong Xinhua Pharmaceutical, which is expected to list by the end of the year.

Analysts said power supplier Beijing Datang Power Generation is expected to raise HK$2.03 to HK$2.45 billion. Although its earnings prospects are bright, investors are expected to focus on other choices in the market.

Medicine maker Shangdong Xinhua should be more attractive since its core business is different from the upcoming infrastructure stocks. Analysts consider its business as high-tech since the company carries out research and development for medicine formulas.
Zhou Xian Power plant, De Zhou Power Plant Co and road firm Shenzhen Freeway are also expected to seek listings in early 1997.
